Adjust the rosewater carefully, as it has a strong aroma that can overpower the cordial if too much is added.
For a festive touch, garnish servings with pomegranate seeds and a sprig of mint.

herb-platter.title: Herb Platter
herb-platter.intro: An Herb Platter is a traditional accompaniment served during Yalda Night, the Persian celebration of the winter solstice. It features a variety of fresh herbs that symbolize renewal and health, complementing the festive spread of fruits, nuts, and sweets.
ingredients: 1 small bowl of sea salt for dipping
steps: Rinse all fresh herbs thoroughly under cold water and pat dry with paper towels.
Arrange the herbs decoratively on a large serving platter, grouping each type separately for easy identification.
Place lemon slices around the edges of the platter for garnish and a touch of color.
Serve the herb platter alongside the main dishes, with a small bowl of sea salt for guests to dip the herbs if desired.
tips: Use the freshest herbs available for the best flavor and aroma.
You can add other seasonal herbs like savory or oregano based on availability and preference.
Serve the herb platter chilled or at room temperature for optimal freshness.

beet-yogurt-dip.title: Beet Yogurt Dip
beet-yogurt-dip.intro: Beet Yogurt Dip is a vibrant and refreshing appetizer traditionally served during Yalda Night, the Persian celebration of the winter solstice. This dip combines the earthy sweetness of beets with creamy yogurt, symbolizing warmth and togetherness as families gather to welcome the longest night of the year.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Fresh dill or mint leaves, for garnish
steps: Place the chopped beets in a pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until tender, about 25-30 minutes.
Drain the beets and let them cool to room temperature.
In a food processor or blender, combine the cooked beets, Greek yogurt, minced garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Season the dip with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Blend briefly again to combine.
Transfer the dip to a serving bowl and drizzle with a little olive oil.
Garnish with fresh dill or mint leaves before serving.
tips: For a smokier flavor, roast the beets instead of boiling them before blending.
Use full-fat Greek yogurt for a richer and creamier dip.
Serve with warm flatbread, pita chips, or fresh vegetable sticks for dipping.

olives-in-pomegranate-molasses.title: Olives in Pomegranate Molasses
olives-in-pomegranate-molasses.intro: Olives in pomegranate molasses is a traditional Iranian appetizer often served during Yalda Night, the winter solstice celebration. This dish combines the tart sweetness of pomegranate molasses with the briny flavor of olives, symbolizing the balance of bitter and sweet in life as families gather to celebrate the longest night of the year.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon (15 ml) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Rinse the olives under cold water and drain well.
In a bowl, combine the pomegranate molasses, olive oil, crushed dried mint, black pepper, and sea salt.
Add the olives to the bowl and toss gently until they are evenly coated with the molasses mixture.
Cover and let marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour to allow flavors to meld.
Before serving, sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley if desired.
tips: Use a mix of green and black olives for a more complex flavor and colorful presentation.
Adjust the amount of pomegranate molasses to taste for more sweetness or tartness.
This dish can be prepared a day ahead to deepen the flavors.

walnut-pomegranate-stew.title: Walnut Pomegranate Stew
walnut-pomegranate-stew.intro: Walnut Pomegranate Stew is a traditional Persian dish often served during Yalda Night, the winter solstice celebration marking the longest night of the year. This rich, tangy, and slightly sweet stew combines the flavors of walnuts and pomegranate molasses, symbolizing fertility and the triumph of light over darkness.
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) stewing beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 cups (480 ml) beef or vegetable broth
Salt and black pepper to taste
Fresh pomegranate seeds and chopped parsley for garnish
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden and translucent, about 7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cinnamon, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beef or lamb cubes and brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the chopped walnuts and mix well.
Pour in the pomegranate molasses and broth, stirring to combine.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer gently for about 1 hour, or until the meat is tender and the stew has thickened.
Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh pomegranate seeds and chopped parsley.
tips: For a vegetarian version, substitute meat with cooked eggplant or mushrooms and use vegetable broth.
Pomegranate molasses can be adjusted to taste for sweetness or tartness; add a teaspoon of sugar if too tart.
Serve with saffron rice or flatbread to soak up the flavorful sauce.

okra-stew.title: Okra Stew
okra-stew.intro: Okra Stew is a hearty and comforting dish traditionally served during Yalda Night, the Iranian celebration of the winter solstice. This stew combines tender okra with tomatoes and aromatic spices, symbolizing warmth and togetherness as families gather to welcome the longest night of the year.
ingredients: 1 cup (240 ml) vegetable or chicken broth
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric, cumin, and cinnamon, cooking for 30 seconds to release their aroma.
Add crushed tomatoes and broth, stirring to combine.
Add the trimmed okra to the pot, stirring gently to coat with the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Bring the stew to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Cook for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until okra is tender and the stew has thickened.
Stir in lemon juice and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
tips: Use fresh okra for the best texture and flavor; frozen okra can be used but may alter the stew's consistency.
Serve the stew with saffron rice or warm flatbread to complete the Yalda Night meal.
For a richer stew, add a handful of cooked chickpeas or lamb pieces during the simmering stage.

shirazi-salad.title: Shirazi Salad
shirazi-salad.intro: Shirazi Salad is a refreshing and tangy Persian salad traditionally served during Yalda Night, the celebration of the winter solstice in Iran. This light salad, made with cucumbers, tomatoes, and onions, symbolizes freshness and renewal as families gather to welcome the longest night of the year.
ingredients: 2 medium cucumbers, finely diced (about 2 cups / 300 g)
3 medium tomatoes, finely diced (about 1 1/2 cups / 225 g)
1 small red onion, finely diced (about 1/2 cup / 75 g)
2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (30 ml)
1/4 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped (15 g)
steps: Wash and finely dice the cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onion into small, uniform pieces.
In a large bowl, combine the diced cucumbers, tomatoes, and onion.
Add the fresh lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and black pepper to the bowl.
Mix the ingredients gently but thoroughly to combine all flavors.
Stir in the chopped fresh parsley and dried mint if using.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or lemon juice if desired.
Refrigerate the salad for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.
tips: Use Persian cucumbers or English cucumbers for a less watery salad.
For added texture, sprinkle some pomegranate seeds on top before serving, which also ties into Yalda Night traditions.
Serve chilled alongside other Yalda Night snacks like nuts, dried fruits, and watermelon.

pomegranate-and-watermelon-fruit.title: Pomegranate And Watermelon Fruit
pomegranate-and-watermelon-fruit.intro: Pomegranate and watermelon are traditional fruits served during Yalda Night, an Iranian festival celebrating the longest night of the year. These fruits symbolize the cycle of life and the warmth of summer, bringing color and sweetness to the festive table.
steps: Cut the watermelon into bite-sized cubes, removing the rind and seeds.
Cut the pomegranates in half and carefully remove the seeds (arils) without breaking them.
In a large serving bowl, combine the watermelon cubes and pomegranate seeds.
If desired, drizzle with fresh lime juice and gently toss to combine.
Sprinkle chopped fresh mint over the fruit mixture for added freshness and aroma.
Serve immediately or chill in the refrigerator for up to 1 hour before serving.
tips: For an attractive presentation, serve the fruit mixture in a hollowed-out watermelon shell.
Add a sprinkle of ground pistachios or a drizzle of honey for extra flavor.
Use fresh, ripe pomegranates and watermelon for the best sweetness and texture.

saffron-rice-cake-with-barberries-and-ch.title: Saffron Rice Cake With Barberries And Chicken
saffron-rice-cake-with-barberries-and-ch.dish: Saffron Rice Cake With Barberries And Chicken
saffron-rice-cake-with-barberries-and-ch.intro: This traditional Persian dish, known as 'Tahchin,' is a festive saffron-infused rice cake layered with tender chicken and tangy barberries. It is often served during Yalda Night, the celebration of the longest night of the year, symbolizing warmth and togetherness with its vibrant colors and rich flavors.
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon ground saffron threads, dissolved in 2 tablespoons hot water
1/4 cup slivered almonds or pistachios (optional, for garnish)
steps: Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear; soak in water for 30 minutes, then drain.
In a pot, bring water to a boil with a pinch of salt; parboil the rice for 5-6 minutes until slightly tender but still firm; drain and set aside.
In a skillet, heat 1 tablespoon oil and sauté the sliced onions until golden and soft; add turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add chicken breasts, salt, and pepper to the skillet; cook until the chicken is fully cooked and lightly browned; remove and shred the chicken once cooled.
In a small pan, melt 1 tablespoon butter; add barberries and sugar, sauté gently for 2-3 minutes until plump; remove from heat and set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, eggs, dissolved saffron with its water, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil.
Add half of the parboiled rice to the yogurt mixture and mix gently to coat the rice evenly.
Grease a 9-inch (23 cm) round baking dish with butter and oil mixture.
Spread half of the saffron-coated rice evenly in the bottom of the dish, pressing down gently to form a layer.
Layer the shredded chicken evenly over the rice, then sprinkle half of the sautéed onions and half of the barberries over the chicken.
Top with the remaining saffron rice, pressing down gently to compact the layers.
Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil and bake in a preheated 350°F (175°C) oven for 1 hour.
Remove the foil and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes to crisp the top layer.
Let the rice cake cool for 10 minutes, then invert onto a serving platter so the golden crust is on top.
Garnish with remaining sautéed onions, barberries, and slivered almonds or pistachios if desired before serving.
tips: Soaking the rice and parboiling helps achieve a fluffy texture and prevents overcooking during baking.
Handle barberries gently as they can be bitter; sautéing with sugar balances their tartness.
For a vegetarian version, substitute chicken with sautéed mushrooms or eggplant.

roasted-nuts-and-dried-fruits.title: Roasted Nuts and Dried Fruits
roasted-nuts-and-dried-fruits.intro: Roasted nuts and dried fruits are a traditional treat served during Yalda Night, an ancient Persian festival celebrating the winter solstice. This mix symbolizes the warmth and light of the sun during the longest night of the year and is enjoyed by families as they gather to share stories and poetry.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Spread the almonds, walnuts, and pistachios evenly on a baking sheet.
Roast the nuts in the oven for 10-12 minutes, stirring halfway through to prevent burning.
While the nuts roast, melt the butter and honey together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Remove the nuts from the oven and transfer them to a mixing bowl.
Pour the honey-butter mixture over the warm nuts and toss to coat evenly.
Add the ground cinnamon and salt, mixing well to distribute the spices.
Allow the nuts to cool slightly, then add the chopped dried apricots, figs, and dried cranberries.
Mix gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve the roasted nuts and dried fruits warm or at room temperature as a festive snack for Yalda Night.
tips: For a spicier mix, add a pinch of ground cardamom or nutmeg.
Use raw, unsalted nuts for the best control over flavor and saltiness.
Store leftovers in an airtight container at room temperature for up to one week.

sesame-topped-barbari-bread.title: Sesame-Topped Barbari Bread
sesame-topped-barbari-bread.intro: Barbari bread is a traditional Persian flatbread known for its thick, chewy texture and distinctive ridges. It is commonly served during Yalda Night, the Iranian festival celebrating the winter solstice, symbolizing warmth and togetherness as families gather to enjoy special foods and poetry.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, and sugar.
In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
Add the yeast mixture and vegetable oil to the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
Divide the dough into two equal parts and shape each into an oval loaf about 12 inches long.
Place the loaves on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Using your fingers or the back of a spoon, create several long, parallel ridges along the surface of each loaf.
Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Prepare the glaze by dissolving the baking soda in lukewarm water.
Brush the glaze generously over the loaves, making sure it fills the ridges.
Sprinkle the sesame seeds evenly over the top of each loaf.
Bake the bread for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Allow the bread to cool slightly before serving.
tips: For a softer crust, brush the bread with melted butter immediately after baking.
You can substitute nigella seeds or a mix of sesame and nigella seeds for a different flavor.
Serve warm with feta cheese, walnuts, and fresh herbs, traditional accompaniments for Yalda Night.

baby-bellini.title: Baby Bellini
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-bellini.intro: The Baby Bellini is a festive, non-alcoholic version of the classic Italian Bellini cocktail, traditionally served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas. This gentle, sparkling peach drink is perfect for all ages and commemorates the innocence and joy of children celebrated on this day.
ingredients: 1 cup (240 ml) peach nectar or peach juice
1 cup (240 ml) sparkling water or non-alcoholic sparkling wine
1 teaspoon (5 ml) honey or simple syrup, optional
steps: Chill the peach nectar and sparkling water in the refrigerator before preparing.
In a large pitcher, combine the peach nectar, fresh lemon juice, and honey or simple syrup if using.
Gently stir the mixture until the honey or syrup is fully dissolved.
Slowly add the sparkling water to the peach mixture to preserve the bubbles.
Pour the Baby Bellini into chilled glasses.
Garnish each glass with a fresh peach slice on the rim.
Serve immediately to enjoy the refreshing fizz.
tips: Use ripe, sweet peaches for the best natural flavor in the nectar or juice.
For a festive touch, rim the glasses with sugar before pouring the drink.
This recipe can be doubled or tripled for larger gatherings.

saffron-rice-pudding.title: Saffron Rice Pudding
saffron-rice-pudding.intro: Saffron Rice Pudding, known as Sholeh Zard, is a traditional Persian dessert often served during Yalda Night, the winter solstice celebration in Iran. This fragrant and vibrant pudding symbolizes light and warmth, bringing comfort during the longest night of the year.
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon ground saffron, dissolved in 2 tablespoons hot water
1/4 cup (35 g) slivered almonds or pistachios for garnish
1/4 cup (35 g) shredded coconut for garnish (optional)
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch.
In a large pot, bring the water to a boil and add the rinsed rice.
Reduce heat to low and simmer the rice uncovered until it is very soft and has absorbed most of the water, about 30 minutes.
Add the sugar to the rice and stir well until fully dissolved.
Pour in the dissolved saffron and rose water, stirring continuously to combine.
Add the butter and continue to cook on low heat, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until the pudding thickens to a creamy consistency, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove from heat and pour the pudding into serving bowls or a large dish.
Sprinkle the top with ground cinnamon, and garnish with slivered almonds or pistachios and shredded coconut if using.
Allow the pudding to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
tips: Use high-quality saffron for the best aroma and color; soak it in hot water to release its flavor.
For a richer pudding, you can substitute 1 cup of water with milk or add a splash of cream at the end.
Garnish creatively with rose petals or dried fruits for an elegant presentation during Yalda Night.

baby-beet-bisque.title: Baby Beet Bisque
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-beet-bisque.intro: Baby Beet Bisque is a velvety, vibrant soup traditionally served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet, commemorating the innocent children. This comforting dish symbolizes purity and renewal, making it a fitting starter for this solemn yet hopeful celebration.
ingredients: 1 pound (450 g) baby beets, peeled and chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped baby beets and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until beets are tender, about 25 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly, then puree the soup in batches using a blender until smooth.
Return the soup to the pot and stir in heavy cream, thyme, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Heat gently over low heat until warmed through, do not boil.
Ladle the bisque into bowls and garnish with chopped fresh chives before serving.
tips: Roast the baby beets beforehand for a deeper, sweeter flavor.
Use coconut cream instead of heavy cream for a dairy-free version.
Add a dollop of sour cream or crème fraîche for extra richness.

baby-greens-salad.title: Baby Greens Salad
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-greens-salad.intro: Baby Greens Salad is a fresh, vibrant dish traditionally served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet, which commemorates the children martyred in Bethlehem. This simple yet elegant salad symbolizes innocence and purity, making it a fitting accompaniment to the solemn yet hopeful occasion.
ingredients: 1/4 cup thinly sliced red onion (about 30 g)
3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (45 ml)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: In a large salad bowl, combine the baby greens, cherry tomatoes, and sliced red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, honey, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese and toasted walnuts over the top before serving.
tips: Use a variety of baby greens such as spinach, arugula, and baby kale for more texture and flavor.
For a nut-free version, substitute walnuts with toasted pumpkin seeds or omit entirely.
Add thinly sliced cucumber or radishes for extra crunch and freshness.

herb-roasted-cornish-hens.title: Herb-Roasted Cornish Hens
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
herb-roasted-cornish-hens.intro: Herb-Roasted Cornish Hens are a traditional centerpiece for the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet, celebrated on December 28th. This dish symbolizes innocence and purity, honoring the children remembered on this solemn day, while offering a comforting and festive meal for family and friends.
ingredients: 2 Cornish hens (about 1 to 1.25 lbs each, 450-570 g)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Rinse the Cornish hens and pat them dry with paper towels.
In a small bowl, combine olive oil, salt, pepper, rosemary, thyme, and minced garlic to create an herb paste.
Rub the herb mixture all over the hens, including inside the cavity.
Stuff each hen’s cavity with lemon quarters and a sprig of parsley.
Place the hens breast side up in a roasting pan and pour chicken broth into the bottom of the pan.
Roast the hens in the preheated oven for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and the skin is golden and crispy.
Baste the hens occasionally with pan juices during roasting to keep them moist.
Remove the hens from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
tips: For extra flavor, marinate the hens in the herb mixture for 2-4 hours before roasting.
Serve with roasted root vegetables or a winter salad to complement the festive meal.
If fresh herbs are unavailable, use 1 teaspoon each of dried rosemary and thyme, but reduce quantity slightly as dried herbs are more concentrated.

duck-fat-roasted-baby-potatoes.title: Duck-Fat Roasted Baby Potatoes
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
duck-fat-roasted-baby-potatoes.intro: Duck-Fat Roasted Baby Potatoes are a rich and flavorful side dish traditionally served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet. This feast commemorates the innocent children lost, and the dish's comforting warmth symbolizes care and remembrance during the holiday.
ingredients: 2 pounds (900 g) baby potatoes, halved if large
1/2 teaspoon (1 g) freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon (15 ml) fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, toss the baby potatoes with the duck fat, kosher salt, black pepper, rosemary, and minced garlic until evenly coated.
Spread the potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper or a roasting pan.
Roast in the preheated oven for 40-45 minutes, turning the potatoes halfway through, until they are golden brown and crispy on the outside and tender inside.
Remove from the oven and sprinkle with fresh parsley if desired before serving.
tips: For extra crispiness, parboil the potatoes for 5 minutes before roasting and drain well.
If duck fat is unavailable, use goose fat or a high-quality olive oil as a substitute, though the flavor will differ.
Add a pinch of smoked paprika or a squeeze of lemon juice after roasting for a flavor twist.

braised-baby-onions.title: Braised Baby Onions
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
braised-baby-onions.intro: Braised Baby Onions are a traditional side dish often served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet, celebrated on December 28th. This dish symbolizes purity and innocence with its delicate flavor and tender texture, making it a fitting accompaniment to the solemn yet festive meal honoring the children commemorated on this day.
ingredients: 1 cup (240 ml) vegetable or chicken broth
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until melted and hot.
Add the peeled baby onions and sauté gently for about 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until they begin to brown lightly.
Pour in the broth, white wine vinegar, and sprinkle the sugar over the onions.
Bring the liquid to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cover the skillet.
Cook gently for 20-25 minutes, or until the onions are tender and the liquid has reduced to a glaze.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
tips: For a richer flavor, substitute half of the broth with dry white wine.
If baby onions are unavailable, pearl onions can be used as a substitute after peeling.
Serve these onions alongside roasted meats or poultry traditionally enjoyed at the Childermas banquet.

slow-smoked-baby-back-ribs.title: Slow-Smoked Baby Back Ribs
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
slow-smoked-baby-back-ribs.intro: Slow-smoked baby back ribs are a hearty and flavorful dish often served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet. This feast commemorates the biblical story of the Holy Innocents, and the rich, comforting ribs symbolize warmth and community during this solemn yet celebratory occasion.
ingredients: 2 racks baby back ribs (about 3 pounds / 1.4 kg each)
1/2 cup barbecue sauce (120 ml), for glazing
Wood chips for smoking (hickory or applewood preferred)
steps: Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs for better smoke penetration.
In a bowl, combine brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, kosher salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper to make the dry rub.
Generously coat both sides of the ribs with the dry rub, pressing it into the meat.
Preheat your smoker to 225°F (107°C) and add wood chips according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Place the ribs bone side down on the smoker rack and smoke for 3 hours, maintaining a steady temperature.
After 3 hours, wrap the ribs tightly in aluminum foil with the apple juice inside to keep them moist.
Return the wrapped ribs to the smoker and cook for an additional 1 hour.
Carefully remove the ribs from foil and brush them with barbecue sauce.
Place the ribs back on the smoker for 15-30 minutes to set the glaze and develop a sticky finish.
Remove from smoker, let rest for 10 minutes, then slice between the bones and serve.
tips: Soak wood chips in water for at least 30 minutes before smoking to create flavorful smoke.
For a spicier kick, increase cayenne pepper or add chili powder to the rub.
If you don't have a smoker, you can cook the ribs low and slow in the oven at 225°F (107°C) and finish under the broiler with barbecue sauce.

baby-corn-gratin.title: Baby Corn Gratin
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-corn-gratin.intro: Baby Corn Gratin is a creamy, cheesy baked vegetable dish traditionally served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet. This dish symbolizes innocence and purity, fitting for a celebration honoring the children. It combines tender baby corn with a rich béchamel sauce and a golden crust, making it a comforting and festive addition to the holiday table.
ingredients: 2 cups baby corn, fresh or thawed if frozen (300 g)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium saucepan, melt butter over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes until it forms a smooth paste but does not brown.
Gradually whisk in the warmed milk, continuing to stir until the sauce thickens and is smooth, about 5 minutes.
Season the béchamel sauce with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.
Add the baby corn to the sauce and stir to coat evenly.
Transfer the mixture to a greased baking dish (about 8x8 inches or 20x20 cm).
In a small bowl, combine the Gruyère, half of the Parmesan, and panko breadcrumbs.
Sprinkle the cheese and breadcrumb mixture evenly over the baby corn.
Drizzle the olive oil over the topping to help it brown.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, until the top is golden and bubbly.
Remove from oven and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan cheese and chopped parsley if desired.
Serve warm as a side dish during the Feast of the Holy Innocents.
tips: For a richer flavor, substitute half the milk with cream.
Add finely chopped shallots or garlic to the béchamel for extra depth.
Use fresh baby corn when in season for the best texture and sweetness.

milk-rolls-with-whipped-honey-butter.title: Milk Rolls with Whipped Honey Butter
milk-rolls-with-whipped-honey-butter.dish: Milk Rolls with Whipped Honey Butter
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
milk-rolls-with-whipped-honey-butter.intro: Milk Rolls with Whipped Honey Butter are a traditional treat served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas. This festival commemorates the biblical story of the Holy Innocents, and these soft, slightly sweet rolls paired with rich honey butter are a comforting, symbolic food enjoyed at the banquet.
steps: In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm milk and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, and salt.
Add the melted butter, egg, vanilla extract, and the yeast mixture to the dry ingredients.
Mix until a soft dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 8 equal pieces. Shape each piece into a smooth ball.
Place the rolls on a greased baking sheet, cover, and let them rise for another 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake the rolls for 18-20 minutes or until golden brown on top.
While the rolls bake, prepare the whipped honey butter by beating the softened butter until fluffy.
Gradually add honey, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt, continuing to whip until light and creamy.
Serve the warm milk rolls with a generous spread of whipped honey butter.
tips: For extra softness, brush the rolls with melted butter immediately after baking.
You can substitute honey in the dough with maple syrup for a different flavor.
Store leftover rolls in an airtight container and reheat gently before serving.

babycham.title: Babycham Cocktail
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
babycham.intro: Babycham is a sparkling perry (pear cider) that originated in England and became popular as a celebratory drink. It is often enjoyed during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas, where it adds a light, festive touch to the banquet honoring the memory of the children. This simple cocktail recipe enhances Babycham with fresh fruit for a refreshing holiday toast.
ingredients: 1 bottle (750 ml) Babycham sparkling perry, chilled
1 cup (150 g) fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
steps: Place the sliced strawberries and lemon slices in a large pitcher.
Pour the chilled Babycham over the fruit.
Gently stir to combine and chill in the refrigerator for 10 minutes if desired.
Pour the Babycham cocktail into chilled glasses.
Garnish each glass with a fresh mint leaf before serving.
tips: Use fresh, ripe strawberries for the best flavor.
For a slightly sweeter drink, add a teaspoon of honey or simple syrup before stirring.
Serve immediately after garnishing to preserve the bubbles in the Babycham.

baby-cheesecakes.title: Baby Cheesecakes
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-cheesecakes.intro: Baby Cheesecakes are a traditional sweet treat served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas, celebrated on December 28th. These small, delicate cheesecakes symbolize innocence and are enjoyed as part of the festive banquet honoring the children remembered on this day.
ingredients: 8 mini graham cracker crusts or tartlet shells
steps: Preheat the oven to 325°F (160°C).
In a medium bowl, beat the cream cheese and sugar together until smooth and creamy.
Add the egg and vanilla extract, mixing until fully incorporated.
Fold in the sour cream gently until the mixture is smooth.
Spoon the cheesecake filling evenly into the mini graham cracker crusts or tartlet shells.
Place the filled crusts on a baking sheet and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the centers are set but still slightly jiggly.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
Before serving, dust with powdered sugar and garnish with fresh berries if desired.
tips: Use full-fat cream cheese for the creamiest texture.
Mini tartlet shells can be homemade or store-bought for convenience.
For a festive touch, add a pinch of cinnamon or nutmeg to the filling.

baby-bananas-foster.title: Baby Bananas Foster
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-bananas-foster.intro: Baby Bananas Foster is a delightful dessert traditionally served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet. This rich, caramelized banana dish symbolizes sweetness and innocence, making it a fitting tribute during this solemn yet celebratory holiday.
ingredients: 8 baby bananas (about 1 pound or 450 grams), peeled
steps: In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the mixture becomes syrupy, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the baby bananas to the skillet and cook gently for 2-3 minutes on each side until they start to soften and caramelize.
Remove the skillet from heat and carefully add the rum.
Return the skillet to low heat and ignite the rum with a long lighter or match to flambé, allowing the flames to subside naturally.
Stir in the vanilla extract and gently coat the bananas with the sauce.
Serve the baby bananas foster warm over scoops of vanilla ice cream.
tips: Use ripe but firm baby bananas to prevent them from becoming too mushy during cooking.
If you prefer not to flambé, simply simmer the rum in the sauce for 1-2 minutes to cook off the alcohol.
For added texture, sprinkle chopped toasted pecans or walnuts over the finished dish.

warm-milk-punch.title: Warm Milk Punch
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
warm-milk-punch.intro: Warm Milk Punch is a traditional festive drink often served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas. This comforting beverage combines warm milk with spices, sugar, and a splash of brandy or rum, symbolizing warmth and celebration during the winter holiday.
ingredients: 1/2 cup brandy or dark rum (120 ml)
steps: In a medium saucepan, combine the milk, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.
Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it is hot but not boiling, about 8 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from heat and stir in the vanilla extract and brandy or rum.
Ladle the warm milk punch into mugs or heatproof glasses.
If desired, top each serving with a dollop of whipped cream and a light sprinkle of grated nutmeg.
Serve immediately while warm.
tips: Use whole milk for a richer, creamier texture; you can substitute with half-and-half for extra richness.
Adjust the amount of brandy or rum to taste, or omit for a non-alcoholic version.
For a smoother texture, strain the punch before serving to remove any spice sediment.
